articleSummary: As of May 15, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is grappling with a significant Ebola outbreak in Ituri Province, reporting 246 suspected cases and 80 deaths, including four confirmed fatalities linked to the Bundibugyo strain. The outbreak is concentrated in the health zones of Mongwalu, Rwampara, and Bunia, exacerbated by humanitarian crises and armed conflict. The index case was a nurse who succumbed to severe symptoms. The World Health Organization (WHO) has allocated $500,000 for containment efforts and is deploying experts to assist local health workers. Additionally, an imported case in Uganda has prompted urgent cross-border coordination among health authorities from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. The Africa CDC has emphasized the need for enhanced surveillance and response measures due to the high risk of further transmission, particularly in urban areas with significant population movement. This outbreak marks the 17th since 1976, following a previous outbreak that ended five months ago with 43 deaths.

articleHeadline: Japanese Encephalitis in Vietnam: Recent cases highlight urgent need for vaccination
articleSummary: In Ho Chi Minh City, two children, aged 9 and 5, were hospitalized in a coma due to Japanese encephalitis (JE), marking a concerning trend in the region. The 9-year-old, who had received partial vaccination, experienced a rapid decline in health over two weeks, leading to neurological deficits and ongoing seizures despite intensive care. The unvaccinated 5-year-old presented with fever and vomiting before deteriorating into seizures and coma, necessitating emergency treatment. These cases are part of four reported JE incidents this year at the hospital, with previous cases resulting in severe long-term neurological issues. The World Health Organization emphasizes the critical nature of rapid medical intervention, as 30-50% of JE survivors face lasting neurological complications. With no specific antiviral treatment available, vaccination is crucial for prevention. The recommended vaccination schedule includes an inactivated mouse-brain vaccine with three initial doses and boosters every three years until age 15, or a recombinant vaccine starting at 9 months with a booster after 12 months. Parents are urged to verify their children's vaccination status.

articleSummary: As of May 15, 2026, Nanchang City CDC reports a significant increase in herpangina cases, a highly contagious enterovirus infection predominantly affecting preschool children under six years old. articleHeadline: Hepatitis A in India: Contamination linked to wastewater management issues
